issue.title: Retire R8 legacy-child dependency readers after a week of zero legacy children

task_type_fields.proposal:
Retire the R8 legacy-child dependency readers that epic bob-cli-3n kept for one release (docs/task-dependencies.md §10 "Legacy window"). Once `bob task-status-hooks --dry-run -f json` reports `legacy_dependency_children: 0` across a week of live hooks runs, remove:

- bob-cli: the R8 legacy-children reader (`src/native/task_dependencies/legacy.rs`), its use in promotion edges (`task_status_hooks/references.rs` dependency_edges), the R8 branches of the R1-R10 reconcile engine (`task_status_hooks/reconcile.rs`: adoption skipping covered ids, legacy count/report key), and the `legacy_dependency_children` output key (or keep it pinned at 0 for one more release, per the contract).
- bob-plugins navigation-hotkeys: `parseDependencyTransclusionBulletDetails` / `parseDependencyLegacyChildDetails` and the legacy fold inside `planDependencyEdit`, the R8 part of `recoveryDependencyReferences`, plus any surviving legacy sync helpers.
- Update docs/task-dependencies.md (§4 R8, §10) and the DP/DW/DR vectors that exercise legacy children, and the decision record's legacy-window wording if it states a date.

Proposed by bob-cli-3n.11 (publish phase, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1). The vault migration (bob-cli-3n.10) already folded all 34 legacy children into Depends-On lines (hooks legacy count 14 -> 0 on 2026-10-02), but the MacBook (the only hooks cron runner) was unreachable and had not yet been updated, so the week of live zero-legacy runs has not started.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-3n deliberately kept the legacy readers for one release so a mixed fleet (the MacBook's older hooks) and any unmigrated note keep working; removing them before a week of zero-legacy runs would contradict its own rollout contract. It is a time-gated cleanup after the epic, not remaining epic work.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-3n.11 proposed removing the one-release legacy-child readers once hooks report zero legacy children for a week; the epic's own rollout contract keeps them until then, so the cleanup is a separate, time-gated task.
